defects: The film is one 15 s locked-off shot. 10 of 14 seconds read as near-identical to the previous second, so pace and change are effectively zero.

In the pairs taken 1/6 s apart, frames are almost static: only a 1–2 px drift and small opacity changes on the margin notes ('yes.' fades in). There is no visible easing, overshoot, weight or motion blur.

The red vertical rule breaks and steps where the stacked panel tiles meet (around y=360 and y=720), and the panels drift a few pixels out of line with each other. This reads as a compositing seam, not a design choice.
The end-card and lockup ('Margin' / 'Edits in the margin.' / margin.app) appears twice, in neighbouring panels, cropped differently. This looks like a duplicated layout, not an intentional rhyme.
The strike-through lines on 'mess' and 'very' are flat red bars with no hand-drawn stroke reveal or pen quality. They sit on top of the glyphs with no interaction.
The faded margin notes ('yes.', 'honest.') have weak contrast against the cream background and are close to unreadable at small sizes.

The audio has a tonal, piano/pluck-like bed with evenly spaced transients and two isolated broadband ticks (~0.9 s and ~5.4 s). The ticks do not line up with any cut, because the film has no cuts. The track stays at one density with no build and ends in a plain fade.
gaps: Motion: there is no choreography. Top studio work would animate the editorial idea itself: live strike-throughs drawn like a pen, words being cut and the line re-flowing with eased kerning, margin notes written in. This film tiles near-static type cards and drifts them.
Pacing and structure: one unbroken 15 s grid with no hierarchy shifts, scale changes, transitions or hero moment. The 'Margin' reveal gets no build or payoff, and the duplicated end-cards dilute it.

Sound and finish: the music is a generic, even bed with nothing designed to the action (no pen scratches, paper sounds or hits on the strike-throughs). The panel seams and broken rule mean the frame would not survive a 100% finishing review, even though the type itself is cleanly anti-aliased.
